rows.subtype: Restless at work and searching for stimulation [Actor]
rows.description: An adult who is not challenged fills the day with small distractions and feels vaguely guilty; boredom asks for meaning, difficulty or rest, depending on cause.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17

rows.subtype: Lost in a game or puzzle [Actor]
rows.description: A child works on a building set, forgetting food and time, with challenge matching skill; the joy of full absorption builds concentration.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager practising guitar or cricket forgets the phone and feels calm and clear afterwards; flow comes when a task is hard enough to need attention but not so hard that it frustrates.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: An adult sets clear goals, reduces interruptions and picks tasks slightly above current skill; conditions that invite flow are usually built and not stumbled upon.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A child who has been scolded or unable to master a task no matter what they do stops trying and says whatever; when effort seems to change nothing, passivity feels sensible.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Not asking for help at home [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager who grew up where their wishes were ignored no longer voices them and waits passively; the belief that nothing they do matters may persist even when things have changed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teacher sees a capable student declare defeat before starting and assigns a small task they can succeed at; success experiences slowly break the belief that effort is useless.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Stuck in an unresponsive job or home [Actor]
rows.description: An adult in a situation where every request has been ignored stops asking and feels numb; if the mood is heavy or lasts, talking to a qualified professional is a sensible step.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child who gets to decide and see the result, such as planting a seed or fixing a toy, learns that actions matter; agency grows from evidence that effort changes things.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager facing a hard family situation lists what is in their control, such as study time and who to talk to, and what is not; acting on the first list restores a sense of power.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22
